subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the sessions.activity API lands, or should core expose activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new core config, delivery mechanisms, privacy boundaries, UI affordances, webhook behavior, and optional model calls, so automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Design lean core watchdog after #39127
options.body: Keep the issue open and implement a default-off metadata-only watchdog only after the public activity contract is defined.

options.title: Expose signals and route alerts to plugins
options.body: Keep core limited to activity and diagnostic signals while ClawHub plugins or dashboards own delivery, summaries, and per-operator policy.

options.title: Defer until activity PRs settle
options.body: Pause implementation until #39127, #96672, or #92697 clarifies the minimum activity/status surface maintainers want to support.

recommendation.title: Design lean core watchdog after #39127
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and implement a default-off metadata-only watchdog only after the public activity contract is defined.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest available owner signal because the canonical prerequisite activity API issue is assigned there and the current gateway activity boundary is in that area.
